# Frontend rules (Next.js 16, App Router)
- Use pnpm only (`pnpm --dir frontend ...`); never npm or yarn, never commit another lockfile.
- Dependency install scripts are blocked by default; allow or deny each one explicitly in `frontend/pnpm-workspace.yaml`
  (`allowBuilds`) and say why. `unrs-resolver: false` is deliberate (prebuilt binaries are used).
- TypeScript strict; no `any`, no `@ts-ignore` without a comment explaining why.
- Server Components by default; add `"use client"` only for state, effects or browser APIs, as low in the tree as possible.
- Routes live in `src/app/`; reusable UI in `src/components/` (kebab-case file names, named exports).
- Call the backend only through `src/lib/api/client.ts` (openapi-fetch). Never hand-write API types:
  `src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` is generated by `gen:api` and gitignored.
- Handle both `data` and `error` from API calls; show `error.detail` from the problem response.
- Secrets never go in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variables or client components.
- Accessible markup: labelled inputs, semantic elements, roles that tests can query.

## Frontend tests
- Vitest + Testing Library; test file next to the component: `name.test.tsx`.
- Query by role / label text, not by CSS class or test id; test behaviour, not implementation.
- Mock `@/lib/api/client` in component tests; never call the real backend.
- Before finishing: `pnpm --dir frontend lint`, `typecheck` and `test` all pass.
